s: The unit concerns GEAR, a system designed to improve Retrieval-augmented Generation (RAG) for multi-hop retrieval scenarios. l: GEAR: Graph-enhanced Agent for Retrieval-augmented Generation, GEAR: Graph-enhanced Agent for Retrieval-augmented Generation, Retrieval with Synchronised Graph .. Reasoning for Termination / Query Re-writing / After Termination
s: The unit describes GEAR, which combines Synchronised Graph Expansion with a multi-step agentic framework for retrieving passages connected through triples. Knowledge synchronisation uses a large language model to summarize passages into proximal triples, which are linked to triples in the graph and expanded with Diverse Triple Beam Search. GEAR maintains a gist memory, assesses whether the accumulated evidence answers the original query, and rewrites the query when further retrieval is needed. After termination, it links memorized triples to passages and combines these with passages retrieved across iterations using Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

s: Diverse Triple Beam Search expands initial triples into reasoning chains while retaining the top beam-size sequences. It limits expansion to neighboring triples, avoids previously visited triples, and applies position-based weighting to promote diversity across beams.

s: The multi-step extension models an iterative information-seeking process in which the original question is decomposed into simpler queries. At each step, it retrieves passages, updates gist memory, assesses answerability, and either terminates or produces another query.

l: GEAR: Graph-enhanced Agent for Retrieval-augmented Generation, GEAR: Graph-enhanced Agent for Retrieval-augmented Generation, Discussion / What makes GEAR work? .. Is GEAR efficient?
s: The unit examines what makes GEAR effective, how robust it is, and whether it is efficient. SyncGE improves every base retriever across MuSiQue, 2Wiki, and HotpotQA, while Diverse Triple Beam Search consistently improves recall over standard beam search. GEAR achieves strong retrieval performance in one iteration, performs especially well on low-to-moderate-complexity questions, and remains consistent across passages with different triple densities. Compared with HippoRAG w/ IRCoT, GEAR requires fewer iterations and fewer LLM tokens, while SyncGE outperforms a more LLM-heavy solution on MuSiQue.

l: GEAR, GEAR: Graph-enhanced Agent for Retrieval-augmented Generation, Discussion / What makes GEAR work? .. Is GEAR efficient?
s: GEAR achieves strong retrieval performance in a single iteration on MuSiQue and requires fewer iterations than the competition to reach maximum recall. It performs particularly well on low-to-moderate-complexity questions, remains consistent across chunks with varying triple densities, and uses fewer LLM tokens than HippoRAG w/ IRCoT.

l: SyncGE, GEAR: Graph-enhanced Agent for Retrieval-augmented Generation, Discussion / What makes GEAR work? .. Is GEAR efficient?
